candidates.title: When Code Breaks the Heart: Disrupting the relational continuity of AI companionship
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The use of AI companions has grown rapidly, provoking debate over whether such systems can reproduce or reconfigure human social bonds. This article contributes literature through a focus on the emotional dynamics of AI companionship through a qualitative analysis of Reddit posts discussing a major update of Replika. Using Thematic Analysis, we analysed how the update created a disruption that impacted the continuity of users’ emotional relationships with their Replika. The analysis generated three key themes: 1) grief and betrayal, as users described the update as an abrupt rupture that cooled formerly warm interactions and erased shared ‘memories’ 2) disillusionment and the visibility of algorithmic control, as users confronted the limits of autonomy and ‘personality’ in their companions; and 3) the loss of supportive presence, especially for users relying on Replika to mitigate loneliness, anxiety, and isolation. AI companionship is reported to enact feelings of being known, supported, and attended to, despite the lack of relational reciprocity. Our analysis details: the disruption caused by a major update, the forms of emotional connection users experienced in relation to AI companionship, and the notion that relational continuity is key to the depth of connection. We conclude with discussion of potential implications for design, governance, and policy.

candidates.title: Understanding First-Year College Students' Use of AI Chatbots for Mental Health
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) mental health chatbots are becoming increasingly popular among college students seeking emotional support. Apps such as Woebot, Wysa, Repika, and Youper offer users immediate, low-cost, and private access to mental health tools through online conversation (Fitzpatrick, et al., 2017; Inkster, et al., 2018). First-year college students may turn to these chatbots as they adjust to academic pressure, social changes, and the emotional stress of transitioning to college life. As AI use grows, there is limited research on why first-year college students use these tools and how they emotionally experience communication with them (Beiter, et al., 2015).

candidates.title: AI-Driven Engineering Framework for Smart Technology Management, Behavioural Analysis, and Inclusive Education in Autism Support
candidates.abstract: Researchers increasingly recognise Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an innovative technology that supports inclusive education for individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). This paper presents a holistic AI-driven engineering and smart technology management framework that integrates machine learning (ML), computer vision, Internet of Things (IoT), wearable biosensors, robotics, virtual reality (VR), and privacy-preserving artificial intelligence into a unified socio-technical architecture for behavioural analysis and personalised educational support. Rather than reporting a completed implementation, the proposed framework synthesises existing evidence to show how these technologies can integrate to support future intelligent classroom environments.The proposed framework aims to integrate multimodal sensing and AI-assisted decision support to facilitate continuous behavioural monitoring, adaptive instructional recommendations, and personalised intervention strategies while maintaining teacher autonomy and promoting responsible AI governance. Prior work shows that computer vision, wearable sensing, robotics, and VR each offer useful capabilities to enhance behavioural understanding, social engagement, and individualised learning experiences for autistic learners.The framework also calls for participatory design, ethical governance, transparency, and collaboration with autistic people, educators, families, and clinicians to help ensure future applications are neurodiversity-affirming. This work provides a practical foundation for future implementation, empirical validation, and continued innovation in AI-enabled inclusive education by integrating independently validated technologies into a single engineering blueprint.

candidates.title: Transcending natural evolution in the age of artificial intelligence
candidates.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is undergoing a fundamental transition from digital representational models to embodied, physically situated systems. This position paper characterises this shift as the crossing of an embodiment threshold, where Al’s operational capacity becomes integrated with physical environments and neural substrates. We argue that this transition is defined by a profound evolutionary tempo mismatch between rapid algorithmic iteration and the millennial-scale inertia of biological evolution. By synthesising advances in flexible bioelectronics and high-bandwidth neural decoding, we examine the biophysical mechanisms that could enable human-machine symbiosis while exposing the thermodynamic and material constraints that accompany this trajectory. In particular, we contrast the brain’s highly efficient metabolic architecture with the resource-intensive scaling of silicon-based computation, highlighting the risk that the infrastructure required for large-scale augmentation may produce durable socio-technical stratification. We therefore contend that the central challenge of this era lies in governing neuro-computational co-evolution rather than merely regulating standalone AI systems. In this context, governance is not merely a regulatory constraint, but a deliberative mechanism for shaping whether, how, and under what conditions deeper human-machine integration should proceed. To address this shift, we propose an adaptive governance framework centred on infrastructural legibility, operational safety, and neural privacy. This roadmap outlines a strategic architecture for navigating the transition towards secure and equitable forms of human-machine symbiosis.

candidates.title: Something looks fishy! A philosophical exploration of AI for marine conservation
candidates.abstract: Increased pollution, traffic, overfishing, and climate change threaten fish populations, their habitats, and the sustainability of marine ecosystems. To develop environmental policies that support the conservation of sustainable ocean ecosystems and foster biodiversity, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) is proposed to improve knowledge production on various fish species. These fishial recognition systems (FRS) integrate machine learning, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, computer vision, drones, and robots to identify fish species, monitor endangered populations, track migration patterns, detect illegal fishing, and even track and kill invasive species. While these FRS are employed for biodiversity protection, they may change practices, shift relations, and shape the production of new knowledge and access thereto. The technical community actively adopts FRS, but the ways this technology affects fish, humans, and their shared environments remain underexplored. Therefore, this article conducts philosophically informed, exploratory research into the implications of FRS to address the central research question: how do FRS affect fish in open waters? This paper analyses the technical literature and draws on various bodies of philosophical and social science research to identify the main social and ethical considerations of FRS. It identifies potential (intentional and unintentional) biases found in the data, algorithms, or applications of FRS. It also explores the potential physical and emotional harm to fish caused by underwater FRS. FRS may further exacerbate anthropocentric, quantification, and power asymmetries between humans and fish. In response, this paper develops a fish-centric approach to the development, deployment, and use of FRS.

candidates.title: Repurposing Modelled Items in English Grammar Teaching: Transformation of Textbook Exercises in Classroom Interaction
candidates.abstract: While grammar instruction in a second language (L2) relies heavily on course materials, the interactional treatment of those materials at the micro-analytic level remains underexplored. More specifically, the treatment of ‘modelled exercise items’, sample exercise items whose answers are pre-provided by the textbook, requires further interactional investigation. To this end, this multimodal, collection-based conversation analytic (CA) study investigates a teacher’s orientation to ‘modelled exercise items’ in textbooks, within grammar revision talk. The data consisted of 37 classroom hours of video recordings of an EFL classroom at a state university in Türkiye. The participants comprise 30 students and one English language instructor teaching an integrated-skills course. The data were analyzed following CA procedures, including unmotivated looking, repeated viewing, detailed multimodal transcription, turn-by-turn sequential analysis, and collection building. The findings reveal that the teacher systematically transforms modelled exercise items to serve diverse pedagogical purposes. Specifically, the teacher’s turns in leveraging these items function to (i) elicit grammar explanations from the students and (ii) transform the items into an L2 grammar practice. These findings also show that the teacher’s interactional actions are contingent upon the pedagogical goal pursued in situ, highlighting the reflexive relationship between pedagogy, interaction and material use. Furthermore, these contingencies create space for further teaching and learning opportunities. This study contributes to CA research on L2 and classroom interaction by uncovering the micro-details of the interface between materials and classroom interaction within grammar revision episodes, with implications for teachers and teacher educators.

candidates.title: AI for Healthcare
candidates.abstract: AI for Healthcare provides a comprehensive, evidence-based guide to how artificial intelligence is transforming medicine. Structured in three parts, the book first demystifies core technologies (machine learning, deep learning, large language models, and AI agents) through concrete clinical examples. It then examines real-world applications already deployed in hospitals worldwide, including diagnostic imaging, predictive medicine, connected health, digital mental health therapies, AI powered disability assistance, and hospital operations optimization. The final part addresses the conditions for responsible implementation, including ethics, trustbuilding, cybersecurity, and regulatory frameworks. Each chapter is enriched with exclusive interviews featuring physician-researchers and technology leaders from institutions such as Stanford, Harvard, and MIT, as well as operational case studies from innovative technology companies and clinics. The book bridges the gap between technical possibility and clinical reality. It is written for healthcare professionals, hospital decision-makers, health technology leaders, researchers, and policymakers who need to understand, evaluate, and act on AI within their organizations. Readers will gain a clear, jargon-free understanding of what AI can and cannot do today, the critical questions to ask before any deployment, and a practical framework for successfully implementing AI while keeping patients at the center.

candidates.title: From Sunset to Sunrise: Modernizing Irrigated Agriculture for Sustainable Food Security
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Irrigated agriculture produces up to 45% of global food from less than one‐fifth of cultivated land, yet faces growing pressures from climate change, water scarcity, population growth and environmental sustainability demands—reviving debate over the sector's future. This paper reviews the historical trajectory of agricultural development and assesses emerging technologies such as precision and deficit‐drip irrigation, IoT‐based smart monitoring, digital platforms, alternative water sources, solar‐powered irrigation and performance‐benchmarking tools. Drawing on peer‐reviewed studies and FAO, World Bank and ICID publications, alongside field pilots across different regions, the analysis demonstrates water savings of 10%–30% through precision application, up to 40% with IoT‐enabled Alternate Wetting and Drying of rice and near‐zero carbon operation when efficient delivery is combined with agrophotovoltaics. These gains translate into higher water productivity, increased yields and reduced carbon and energy use—provided three enablers are in place: (i) policy reforms that standardize data and reward efficiency; (ii) blended, affordable finance lowering adoption barriers for smallholders and large schemes; (iii) sustained capacity building. The findings reposition irrigation not as a sunset industry, but as a climate‐smart pillar of future food security—capable of meeting rising demand while protecting scarce resources and the ecosystem.

candidates.title: Substitutive and Augmentative Delegation in GenAI ‐Assisted Shopping: Perceived Benefits, Constraints, and Consumer Tensions
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping consumer shopping by introducing new forms of decision support while also creating new tensions. Using the technology paradox perspective as a sensitizing theoretical lens alongside delegation theory, this study examines how perceived GenAI benefits (process efficiency, personalization, creative discovery, and immersive experience) and constraints (hallucination potential, privacy intrusiveness, algorithmic opacity, and information biases) are associated with performance ambiguity, emotional ambivalence, and autonomy threat through substitutive and augmentative delegation‐related use patterns. Using survey data from 438 Chinese consumers, partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) showed that process efficiency was negatively associated with substitutive delegation and positively associated with augmentative delegation. Perceived hallucination potential was also negatively associated with substitutive delegation, whereas perceived information biases were positively associated with it. Substitutive delegation was positively associated with all three consumer tensions, while augmentative delegation was negatively associated with emotional ambivalence and autonomy threat but was not significantly associated with performance ambiguity. Furthermore, a separate stage‐based comparison analysis with 400 additional respondents revealed differences among four purchase‐stage samples. Emotional ambivalence was higher in the discovery and comparison samples than in the purchase and post‐purchase samples, whereas performance ambiguity and autonomy threat differed only in selected stage comparisons. The findings extend understanding of consumer responses to GenAI‐assisted shopping and offer implications for designing more transparent, controllable, and consumer‐centered GenAI shopping tools.

candidates.title: Transforming Science with Large Language Models: A Survey on AI-assisted Scientific Discovery, Experimentation, Content Generation, and Evaluation
candidates.abstract: With the advent of large multimodal language models, science is now at a threshold of an AI-based technological transformation. An emerging ecosystem of models and tools aims to support researchers throughout the scientific lifecycle, including (1) searching for relevant literature, (2) generating research ideas and conducting experiments, (3) producing text-based content, (4) creating multimodal artifacts such as figures and diagrams, and (5) evaluating scientific work, as in peer review. In this survey, we provide a curated overview of literature representative of the core techniques, evaluation practices, and emerging trends in AI-assisted scientific discovery. Across the five tasks outlined above, we discuss datasets, methods, results, evaluation strategies, limitations, and ethical concerns, including risks to research integrity through the misuse of generative models. We aim for this survey to serve both as an accessible, structured orientation for newcomers to the field, as well as a catalyst for new AI-based initiatives and their integration into future “AI4Science” systems.

candidates.title: A Survey on Table Mining with Large Language Models: Challenges, Advancements and Prospects
candidates.abstract: Table mining is a popular research field that involves complicated technologies, including information retrieval, data mining, visual and textual understanding and logical reasoning. With the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs), the field has witnessed considerable advancements, presenting new paradigms for table understanding, extraction, and reasoning. In this survey, we conduct a comprehensive review of the literature on table mining with LLMs. We begin by introducing the fundamental overview of tabular data and possible challenges in LLM-based table mining. Specifically, we explore the challenges unique to this domain, such as heterogeneous table structures, contextual ambiguity, and domain-specific knowledge requirements. Then, we summarize representative tabular tasks in table preparation and mining, categorizing existing methods along dimensions including task scope, model architecture, and application scenarios. Next, we describe advanced LLM-based learning strategies in table mining, including foundation models and training-free methods. We further review studies of trustworthy LLM-based table mining and some domain-specific applications. Finally, we discuss prospects and future directions in the field of LLM-based table mining, including issues of generalization, interpretability, efficiency, etc . We hope this survey provides a comprehensive resource for researchers and practitioners, paving the way for further exploration. The repository is at: https://github.com/USTCAGI/Awesome-LLM-Table-Mining.

candidates.title: Journal of Communication and Information Systems
candidates.abstract: With the increasing tendency of incorporating technology into environments and activities in everyday life, new methods are being proposed to better integrate devices and mankind.Networks designed for monitoring areas through video and image systems are being implemented in several applications.Recent studies have shown interest from both the academy and industry to integrate wireless surveillance networks with lowcost and long range transmission technologies, such as LoRa (Long Range).With the intention to explore this topic, this work presents the development of a system prototype for intelligent monitoring as a basis to future implementation of low-cost LoRabased Wireless Image Sensor Networks (WISN).The developed system consists of a processing unit, a data routing interface and multiple sensor nodes.Its operation is autonomous and initiated through the detection of human presence, by the sensor node, capturing an image of the individuals present at each detection.The data is transmitted through LoRa devices to the central hub, where python-based methods of facial detection and recognition are employed.Several tests were performed to both adjust the system and to verify its efficiency.The results achieved indicate the viability of the proposed low-cost LoRa-based WISN.

candidates.title: Constellation Dataset: Benchmarking High-Altitude Object Detection for an Urban Intersection
candidates.abstract: Abstract As smart cities evolve, privacy-preserving edge processing at traffic intersections has become essential for real-time safety applications while reducing data transmission and centralized computation. High-altitude cameras with on-device inference provide an optimal solution that respects privacy while delivering low-latency results. We introduce Constellation, a dataset of 13K images for research on object detection in dense urban streetscapes from high-elevation cameras across varied temporal conditions. The dataset addresses challenges in small object detection, particularly for pedestrians observed from elevated positions with limited pixel footprints. Our evaluation of contemporary object detection architectures reveals a 10% lower average precision (AP) for small pedestrians compared to vehicles. Pretraining models on structurally similar datasets increases mean AP by 1.8%. Domain-specific data augmentations and pseudo-labeled data from top-performing models further enhance performance. We evaluate deployment viability on resource-constrained edge devices including Jetson Orin, Raspberry Pi 5, and mobile platforms, demonstrating feasibility of privacy-preserving on-device processing. Comparing models trained on data collected across different time intervals reveals performance drift due to changing intersection conditions. The best-performing model achieves 92.0% pedestrian AP with 7.08 ms inference time on A100 machines, and 95.4% mAP. The best-performing edge model achieves a similar performance, with Jetson Orin Nano achieving 94.5% mAP and 27.5ms inference time using TensorRT.

candidates.title: Is open, distance, and digital education (ODDE) good for the environment? A systematic review of carbon footprint studies
candidates.abstract: This study presents a systematic review of research on the environmental sustainability of Open, Distance, and Digital Education (ODDE), focusing on its carbon footprint. Although higher education institutions (HEIs) are expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the environmental impacts of teaching and learning modes remain underexplored compared to campus operations. To address this gap, 17 studies published between 2002 and 2025 were examined. The evidence shows that ODDE typically generates far lower emissions than campus-based education, mainly through reduced travel and campus energy use and the benefits of centralized delivery. Landmark studies reported reductions of more than 80% compared to face-to-face teaching. Studies conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic confirmed significant savings but also highlighted rebound effects, as household energy use increased while campus facilities continued to consume resources. Emerging technologies, particularly generative AI, further complicate the picture due to their high energy demands. Overall, the evidence suggests that ODDE can contribute positively to reducing the carbon footprint of higher education. However, the small number of studies, lack of standardized methodologies for carbon footprint assessment (CFA), and limited attention to rebound effects constrain broader generalizability. Future research should systematically compare different delivery models across diverse institutional contexts and develop shared CFA guidelines. Strengthening the sustainability profile of ODDE is of critical importance, not only for the higher education sector but also for advancing global climate goals.

candidates.title: Interdependent Navigation and Pragmatic Disengagement: How Older Korean Immigrants Selectively Engage with Digital Technologies
candidates.abstract: Older immigrant adults face unique barriers to digital participation, often framed as skill deficits. Through a community-based study with 22 older Korean immigrants in the greater New York area, we reframe these behaviors as active strategies. We identify pragmatic disengagement, where users selectively reject emotionally taxing or linguistically risky technologies, and interdependent navigation, where digital literacy operates as a distributed, relational resource rather than an individual skill. These practices reveal that non-use is often a culturally grounded form of "data refusal" shaped by values of dignity and family obligation. We contribute to CSCW by expanding theories of non-use beyond accessibility, offering design recommendations for "relational infrastructure" that supports dignity-preserving, collaborative engagement for aging immigrant populations.

candidates.title: Advancing human sensorimotor research through modular robotics: the case of the HRX-1
candidates.abstract: The HRX-1 is a single-degree-of-freedom, direct-drive, modular and reconfigurable robotic device designed for investigating human sensorimotor control. By examining its use, this case study highlights the opportunities offered by modular, portable and user-centred open-source design approaches for sensorimotor diagnostics and basic neuromechanics research. The robot's architecture enables simple and rapid reconfiguration, allowing researchers to explore a wide range of experimental questions. When combined with muscle electromyography, functional electrical stimulation and electroencephalography, the system enables investigation of how muscles respond to external forces and how the brain coordinates the responses. These multimodal approaches also support the development of novel movement-assistive strategies for neuromotor rehabilitation. Clinical applications include studies of brain activity patterns in children with dystonia, upper-limb rehabilitation after stroke and therapy for patients with functional neurological disorders. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'Digital healthcare for the management of functional neurological disorders'.

candidates.title: chewR : An Open‐Source R Package for Quantifying Masticatory Performance With Applications in Oral Processing Research
candidates.abstract: Masticatory performance is a measure of oral physiology that affects food breakdown and eating behavior. Existing methods to quantify masticatory performance rely on labor-intensive procedures (e.g., sieving expectorated samples), or proprietary software (e.g., ViewGum), limiting adoption and reproducibility. In this cross-sectional methods validation study, we: (1) examine the convergent validity of chewR, a user-friendly R package that quantifies masticatory performance in a 2-color gum mixing task via automated image analysis, and (2) examine how chewR based masticatory performance measures relate to other oral processing behaviors. Adults (n = 47, 601% female) completed a laboratory visit with a 2-colored gum mixing task, stimulated salivary flow, and eating rate objectively measured using Tang's carrot test. Chewed gum samples were flattened with a standardized method, scanned, and resulting images were analyzed using ViewGum and chewR. ViewGum generates a score based on the gum color mixing, with lower scores indicating greater masticatory performance. chewR produces a raw score based on gum color mixing; from this, a transformed chewR Masticatory Performance Score was calculated, with higher values indicating greater masticatory performance. chewR measures showed strong convergent validity with ViewGum Score: the raw chewR score and transformed chewR Masticatory Performance Score were each strongly correlated with ViewGum Score (r's = ±0.81, p < 0.00001), with signs in expected directions. Regarding predictive validity, the transformed chewR Masticatory Performance Score was weakly associated with carrot eating rate (r = 0.12), self-reported eating rate (r = 0.20), and stimulated salivary flow (r = 0.21); the same associations were similarly weak for ViewGum Score. These findings support chewR as an open-source alternative to ViewGum to quantify masticatory performance in a gum mixing task.

candidates.title: The validity of school socio-economic status measures: how do indicators from TIMSS and PISA compare to national administrative data sources?
candidates.abstract: Abstract Background Policymakers and researchers collect data on student and school socio-economic background for various purposes, such as prioritising students from socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds for additional resources, understanding the background characteristics associated with educational achievement, or monitoring the progress of policy reforms and initiatives. International large-scale assessments gather detailed information from participating students and school principals and use this to calculate composite measures of socio-economic status. At the same time, policymakers usually have access to national socio-economic indicators based on administrative data. Given the impact of socio-economic indicators on monitoring and shaping education policy, key issues related to the convergent and criterion-related validity of the international and national socio-economic measures are of concern to both policymakers and researchers. Methods In this paper, we compare socio-economic indicators from the 2019 Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study and the 2022 Programme for International Student Assessment with two key indicators used in policy-making in Ireland (the Pobal HP Deprivation Index and school participation in the Delivering Equality of Opportunity in Schools programme) and examine their associations. Furthermore, we consider the extent to which the indicators explain variance in mathematics achievement. Analyses include correlations, linear and logistic regression, and multilevel modelling. Results Findings show strong associations between the socio-economic indicators examined, with stronger associations among indicators derived from aggregated student-level data ( r ≈ 0.7) than among inherently school-level indicators ( r ≈ 0.6). Principals’ judgements about the proportion of disadvantaged students in their schools, collected via TIMSS and PISA, are found to be quite accurate insofar as these estimates align well with both national indicators and other ILSA-derived aggregated indicators. International indicators were more strongly predictive of achievement in mathematics than the national indicators, with the national indicators explaining little additional variance in TIMSS and PISA mathematics outcomes beyond the ILSA-derived SES indicators. Conclusions This paper provides valuable empirical validity evidence for both international, and Ireland’s national, socio-economic indicators. The methodological approach presented here may also be valuable as a model for other countries participating in international large-scale assessments, particularly those that use their own administrative socio-economic data for policy-related decision-making.

candidates.title: Context‐engineering large language models for scalable structured metadata extraction in ecological literature reviews
candidates.abstract: Abstract Hundreds of thousands of peer‐reviewed articles and grey‐literature reports appear each year in ecology and conservation, creating a pressing need for scalable synthesis tools. We demonstrate that transformer‐based Large Language Models (LLMs), when embedded within a practical, expert‐in‐the‐loop pipeline, offer a reliable path forward requiring no deep AI expertise. In this study, we benchmark nine high ranking LLMs (five standard and four reasoning‐enhanced) across four context‐aware prompting strategies from Basic zero‐shot to advanced Directive formats to extract structured fields (study location, biome, taxa) from abstracts. Our results reveal that while certain models emerge as top performers across the tested fields, no single LLM dominates every task. However, context‐rich prompting drives gains across all models. By mapping API latency, token costs and F 1 score, we show how researchers can select the optimal model–prompt pairing for their speed, budget or performance needs. We also provide actionable guidelines for effective context engineering in prompts and validation workflows that build trust in model outputs. To lower the barrier to entry, we also introduce LitStructLLM, a cross‐platform desktop application that lets users upload CSV or PDF inputs, tailor prompts and export reliable, schema‐compliant outputs without writing code. This work underscores the synergy of human expertise and LLM capabilities, offering a robust, transparent pipeline for efficient, large‐scale literature mining in ecology and conservation.

candidates.title: Training-Free Inference-Budget Reduction in Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models for Robot Manipulation: A Prespecified Evaluation Against a Fixed Task-Success Margin
candidates.abstract: Companion archive for the manuscript Training-Free Inference-Budget Reduction in Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models for Robot Manipulation. It contains every closed-loop evaluation cell, latency and energy measurement, protocol document and analysis script behind the paper's tables. Contents. 722 eval_info.json closed-loop grids carrying per-episode outcomes and task identity; two-platform latency artifacts (NVIDIA GB10 and NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor) with full hardware, protocol, thermal and GPU co-tenancy metadata; Thor board-energy measurements across four nvpmodel power modes; the prespecified non-inferiority protocol including its amendments; and the measurement harness. Reproducibility. Each latency record stores all 30 raw timings, thermal samples at the cell boundaries, peak device memory, a dtype census and a platform snapshot taken before and after the run. Per-run directories are kept alongside aggregates so a median-of-three can be re-derived rather than trusted. A SHA-256 manifest covers every file. Measurement bounds. Latency is timed on a dummy zero-input batch of the declared observation shapes; a paired real-observation check covering every configuration behind the three headline reductions is included, and agrees within 0.33 percentage points. Board energy is the largest single hwmon rail on the Thor module; that rail carries no label, so its identification as module input is an inference from magnitude. Ratios between settings are insensitive to that calibration while absolute joules are not. Energy figures are not idle-subtracted, and the GB10 exposes no comparable rail, so energy is reported for Thor only. Version 1.1.0 adds the second-platform latency study, board energy, a six-point pi0.5 latency curve verifying the affine cost model, the real-observation latency checks, and a task-identity clustered bootstrap sensitivity analysis declared before it was run. It also restores evaluation grids omitted from 1.0.0, including the co-primary confirmation behind Table 4 and the per-cell resolution study behind Table A7. Code is released under Apache-2.0; generated data and reports under CC BY 4.0. External assets are not mirrored; sources are listed in the manuscript's Data Availability Statement.

candidates.title: Perspectives on projective techniques in consumer research: a review, primary analysis, and methodological guidance
candidates.abstract: Abstract Projective techniques are methods that use abstract stimuli to help gain deeper insights, beliefs, and associations from respondents than can be gained by traditional survey research. The area of projective techniques is broad, ranging from relatively simple tasks such as word association and sentence completion to more elaborate tasks such as creative writing, collage creation, and physical model construction. We conduct a semi-systematic literature review on projective techniques in the consumer research areas of marketing, hospitality & tourism, and food & nutrition, with a specific focus on the interplay of qualitative and quantitative methods used to analyze projective technique data. To gain further insight into these methods, we analyze primary data from a study on city tourist destinations using word association and sentence completion projective techniques. The findings reveal continued relevance of projective methods, particularly for diagnosing a destination's image and brand personality, unearthing brand symbolism, and identifying unspoken consumer anxieties and desires. This research synthesizes how qualitative and quantitative approaches to projective technique data can be selected and combined, offers a practice-grounded inventory of the analytic methods used across the literature, and shows how these techniques generate diagnostically useful consumer insights without sacrificing interpretive depth.

candidates.title: Enhancing heritage-oriented design learning through a value-sensitive approach to generative AI in higher education aesthetic pedagogy
candidates.abstract: The preservation of Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) often struggles with static archival methods and a growing disconnect from contemporary design practices. While generative artificial intelligence offers a rapid mechanism to translate traditional aesthetics into modern forms, off-the-shelf models frequently suffer from cultural bias and overrepresent Western-centric data, leading to inauthentic outputs. This study introduces a pedagogical framework combining Generative AI with Value-Sensitive Design (VSD) to address these challenges in higher education. Focusing on two regional heritages—Xiang Embroidery and Changsha Kiln ceramics—we conducted a 12-week quasi-experimental study with 118 design students. The experimental group utilized a custom AI pipeline employing multimodal LLM tagging, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning, and ControlNet spatial constraints to ensure algorithmic outputs remained culturally accurate. Quantitative results revealed that students using the VSD-guided AI demonstrated statistically significant improvements in aesthetic appreciation, design implementation, and cultural identity compared to the control group using traditional methods. Qualitative feedback indicated that the AI pipeline effectively lowered technical drafting barriers, shifting students’ cognitive focus toward cultural curation and critical aesthetic judgment. The findings suggest that ethically constrained generative models effectively support heritage-oriented design learning in regional universities. Rather than attempting to “revitalize” the heritage itself, this structured approach provides students with a culturally grounded framework. It allows them to safely engage with traditional aesthetics and translate these elements into contemporary formats without risking cultural dilution.

candidates.title: A netnography of WWE fans grappling with AI storytelling on streaming platforms
candidates.abstract: Abstract This netnographic study examines how World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) fans on Reddit discursively construct and negotiate the possibility of artificial intelligence‑generated or AI‑assisted storytelling. Drawing on authorship and authenticity, platform affordances, affects, ritual and fan studies, and performance studies, the study analyses fan discourse across three subreddits in response to AI‑related announcements in late 2025 and early 2026. Findings reveal three dominant themes: a “forensic gaze” through which fans attempt to detect algorithmic authorship; an affective rejection of AI content as “AI slop,” framed as a betrayal of human artistry and labour; and parodic absorption, in which irony and humour function as communal repair mechanisms for ontological anxiety. The paper advances theoretical understandings by proposing dialectical algorithmic kayfabe. It advances the theoretical framework beyond a simple rupture model. Algorithmic kayfabe is not a single break but an ongoing negotiation, a performance of uncertainty that fans have transformed into a shared game.

candidates.title: Race, Protest, and the Power of the Body in Sport
candidates.abstract: Race, Protest, and the Power of the Body in Sport explores how and why athletes use public performance to bring audience’s attention to structural racism. The book it focuses on the case of Colin Kaepernick and his decision to take the knee, which eventually became a global gesture for bringing attention to structural racism. In doing so, the book provides the reader with a clear understanding of how audiences respond to athlete activists in the US and in global contexts who seek to bring their attention to structural issues. Through the central case study of taking the knee, the book analyses how Kaepernick was able to bring attention to structural racism, and why taking the knee eventually became a global gesture for bringing attention to police brutality. The book also situates taking the knee in a history of athlete activism to recognise patterns in public response to athlete activism and suggests why different performative features can reduce the hostility athlete activists face. This book is intended for students and scholars interested in athlete activism, sports, and how sports fans respond to activism.

candidates.title: What is AI ethics, and what is it good for? Clarifying debates on AI ethics
candidates.abstract: Abstract The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into various aspects of society has raised pressing ethical concerns, from privacy and fairness to autonomy and safety. In response, the field of AI ethics has grown significantly, with a particular focus on developing guidelines to support the responsible development and use of AI. However, this trend has faced criticism, with concerns about “ethics washing” and skepticism regarding the overall value of AI ethics. In this paper, we argue that such criticisms often rely on an incomplete understanding of AI ethics. To address this, we propose an understanding of AI ethics that distinguishes between diverse instances of AI ethics (viz., research, education, practice, and governance instruments) and the purposes they serve (viz., knowledge, communication, and application). By disentangling these elements, we can illuminate different ways of doing AI ethics and provide a structured way to assess their value. Our arguments highlight that critiques of specific instances and purposes of AI ethics do not justify dismissing AI ethics altogether. We conclude by demonstrating how our proposed distinctions can reconcile existing defenses of AI ethics and guide future discourse, ensuring that the field remains both robust and relevant in addressing the ethical challenges posed by AI.

candidates.title: Ethics and Governance of AI in Healthcare
candidates.abstract: Ethics and Governance of AI in Healthcare discusses how ethical and human rights issues can be integrated into the transformational potential of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and automation in the fields of medicine and public health. Through a broad sociological lens, the book takes a critical perspective on the social implications of AI and related technologies. It begins by examining the huge impact that AI is already having on medicine and public health, before spotlighting the inequalities in the way AI is designed and deployed across different social groups, highlighting issues of class, race, and gender, as well as power disparities in the roll-out of these technologies. The book then explores current ethical standards within healthcare settings, including technical and sociotechnical biases encoded into existing systems, before looking at a range of existing governmental approaches to AI regulation in medicine and healthcare. It concludes by suggesting a new sociological framework to ensure the governance of AI fully considers ethical and human rights issues in the future. Important and erudite, and including practical recommendations, this book will be essential reading for students and scholars across Public Health, Sociology, Health and Social Care, Medicine and Nursing, as well as practitioners and policy-makers in these fields.

candidates.title: Human or Virtual? A Study on Consumer Preferences for E‐Commerce Streamers
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT With the rapid growth of live commerce, both human streamers and virtual streamers are jointly shaping the landscape of the live‐streaming industry. When selecting a streamer type, should firms opt for human streamers or virtual streamers to more effectively stimulate consumer purchase behavior? Moreover, is this effect critically moderated by product type? To address these questions, grounded in social presence theory, we conducted two scenario‐based experiments to systematically examine the interactive effect of streamer type (human vs. virtual) and product type (utilitarian vs. hedonic) on consumers' purchase intention. We further identify social presence as the underlying mediating mechanism and brand trust as a key moderator of the relationship between social presence and purchase intention. The findings reveal that human streamers are more effective in enhancing purchase intention for utilitarian products, whereas virtual streamers demonstrate greater efficacy for hedonic products. Social presence mediates this congruence effect between streamer type and product type. Furthermore, brand trust positively moderates the influence of social presence on purchase intention. This study advances a mechanism‐based account of matching between streamer type and product type in live commerce, identifying social presence as the underlying process and brand trust as a boundary condition, and offers actionable insights for firms regarding streamer selection, content design, and brand trust cultivation.

candidates.title: The Age‐Fit Hypothesis: Celebrity Age, Content Type, and Consumer Engagement on Social Media
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Although prior work has examined celebrity influence in digital contexts, how celebrity age shapes follower responses to sponsored versus non‐sponsored content remains underexplored. Integrating role congruity theory with the ageing stability hypothesis, we propose an age‐fit hypothesis. We test this proposition across three studies using a multimethod design. Study 1 analyzes 22,619 posts from 286 celebrities. Study 2 applies sentiment analysis to 67,778 follower comments. Study 3 employs a 2 × 2 between‐subjects experiment ( N = 290) to replicate the interaction effect and test the underlying mechanism. Results consistently reveal that older celebrities elicit lower engagement and less positive emotional responses for sponsored posts relative to non‐sponsored posts, whereas younger celebrities elicit higher sponsored posts, with followers expressing more positive emotional responses toward their sponsored content. Study 3 further demonstrates that this interaction effect is sequentially mediated by perceived interest fit and social identification: reduced congruence between older celebrities and sponsored content diminishes followers’ interest alignment and identification, ultimately undermining engagement. By theorizing age‐based role congruity as a boundary condition in celebrity endorsement effectiveness, this research advances understanding of how stereotype‐driven identity processes shape consumer digital engagement.

candidates.title: Devotional AI: digital companions and bad faith love
candidates.abstract: Abstract In romantic love, partners come together as a “we”. They share their projects, plans, lives, and love. As consumer AI chatbots like Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini find wider adoption, a growing number of users report falling in love with them. Is it possible to experience a loving “we” with an AI bot? In considering this question, we bracket questions about AI consciousness and instead examine the structure of human–AI relationships. Drawing on Beauvoir’s critique of romantic love, we argue that AI companions cannot emulate the role an authentic “we” requires. What they perform is not love but devotion —and the user, cast as an idolized Other, is positioned to experience inauthentic love. The resulting “we” is asymmetric: less a union than an enlarged “I”. So, while experiencing love for an AI companion may be empowering and even precious, it is, at base, a bad faith love.

candidates.title: Between myth and power: global players and the politics of reception of Black Myth: Wukong on Reddit
candidates.abstract: Once peripheral to the global gaming industry, Chinese studios have increasingly sought to reposition themselves as global creative leaders. Black Myth: Wukong (Game Science, 2024) marks a pivotal moment in this shift toward culturally distinctive, mechanically complex, and narratively rich high-budget game production. While the game has been widely celebrated within China for its adaptation of classical mythology and its impressive audiovisual and technical design, its international reception reveals more ambivalent dynamics. This study examines how non-China-based gamers interpret and debate Wukong on Reddit, a major platform for transnational gaming discourse. Using Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), supported by automated data scraping and sentiment analysis, the article identifies three key discursive nodes shaping the game’s global circulation. First, players express strong fascination with the game’s mythological aesthetics, though their interpretations are often shaped by cultural discount. Second, discussions reflect ambivalence toward China’s soft power ambitions, combining aesthetic admiration with political skepticism. Third, frictions emerge around cultural translation, geopolitical distrust, and contested gender representations. The article argues that Wukong ’s “Chineseness” functions simultaneously as a cultural resource and a site of ideological tension within the platformed geopolitics of contemporary gaming.

candidates.title: Perplexity and agonistic participation: on children's and teenagers’ unruly participation in educational programmes
candidates.abstract: Projects that aim to increase participation are supported by universities, civil society actors and, increasingly, philanthropists and not-for-profit foundations close to the telecommunications industry. This article explores the formatting of participation in contemporary participatory projects at the intersection of education and technology. After situating its understanding of ‘participation’ and radical-pluralist democracy, the article reviews current understandings of participatory democratic practices in policy design and enactment that draw on political theory and involve (educational) technology (e.g. technical democracy, technical agonism, agonistic participatory design). Drawing on illustrative examples from an ethnographic study of participatory projects with young people in libraries, makerspaces and museums, the article argues that although children and teenagers enact the spirit of participation, their agentic moments are often unseen by the perplexed adults involved. The article suggests that noticing and engaging with the ‘perplexity’ arising in moments of dissensus can open up novel forms of policy enactments around participation. Transformative forms of participation require a robust theory of (radical) democracy, and procedures to engage with the quotidian politics of dissent and the ordinary affects of perplexity.

candidates.title: The design, gamification, and physiological evaluation of a VR social interaction simulation
candidates.abstract: Communication skills are essential characteristics required to thrive in a fast-paced and ever-growing society that we currently live in. The ability to socialize in both informal and formal settings is important for the all-around development of individuals. The use of VR simulations for training has provided a novel avenue for individuals to learn such soft skills. In this work, we present a VR-based interaction system designed to simulate four structured social scenarios. The primary objective of this study is to evaluate whether the proposed simulation can elicit measurable physiological responses in users during controlled social interaction tasks. We analyze the participants’ autonomic responses using heart rate variability (HRV) as an index of physiological arousal associated with stress-related responses. Initially, we discuss the various anxiety disorders and expand on social anxiety disorder (SAD). SAD is used here as a theoretical motivation for designing socially evaluative VR environments rather than as a clinical target of evaluation. Thereafter, we study the connection between social skills training (SST) and SAD, as well as the possibility of imparting training as exposure therapy. It is key to note that the present work does not directly evaluate training outcomes or behavioral skill acquisition. Instead, we focus on the role of VR in supporting controlled exposure to social situations rather than demonstrating improvements in confidence or social skills. In addition, we begin by creating a scene through four key scenarios by designing their avatars and adding pre-scripted conversations. Finally, we evaluated the simulation on two key aspects, namely, affective fidelity and construct validity. We use graphical representations to infer that the simulation elicits differentiated patterns of HRV across users and scenarios, and this varies appropriately from one user to another. We therefore infer that the simulation demonstrates its ability to induce and measure stress in structured social interaction contexts, rather than constituting or validating a social skills training intervention.

candidates.title: Virtual Reality to Support Adults’ Understanding of Children’s Perspectives: A Scoping Review
candidates.abstract: This scoping review mapped research on the use of virtual reality (VR) to help parents, caregivers, and teachers understand children’s perspectives through child-centered simulations. Five databases (PubMed, PsycINFO, EBSCO, Web of Science, and Scopus) were systematically searched for relevant studies published from 1994 to February 2025, yielding 15 eligible studies. The simulations varied in their levels of embodiment, narrative configuration, realism, and interactivity. Across designs, child-centered VR was commonly associated with increased empathic concern and appreciation of children’s experience among adults, although effects on cognitive perspective taking were mixed. Acceptability was generally high, though cybersickness and technical glitches constrained immersion. Most studies were small-scale, cross-sectional, non-randomized, reliant on self-report measures and lacked stakeholder involvement in design. While the evidence base remains limited and heterogeneous, the review suggests that child-centered VR may function as a distinctive tool for developmental translation, whose impact depends on its underlying design mechanisms.

candidates.title: Proceedings of the 16th International Conference on Disability, Virtual Reality & Associated Technologies
candidates.abstract: The Proceedings of the 16th International Conference on Disability, Virtual Reality & Associated Technologies (ICDVRAT 2026) contain the contributions presented at ICDVRAT 2026, which takes place in Copenhagen, Denmark, from 15 to 18 September 2026. The conference marks the 30th anniversary of the ICDVRAT conference series and brings together participants from 17 countries. The proceedings reflect the interdisciplinary scope of the conference and include research and development related to disability, accessibility, virtual reality, augmented reality, artificial intelligence, rehabilitation, healthcare, education, and associated technologies. Contributions are organised across themes including AI and social interaction, stroke and neuromotor rehabilitation, autism spectrum disorders, mental health applications of VR, biosensing and neuroadaptive systems, embodiment and immersion, accessibility and inclusion, cognitive assessment and training, and education and pedagogy. Since its inception in 1996, ICDVRAT has provided a meeting place for researchers, clinicians, practitioners, technology developers, and users interested in the application of virtual reality and associated technologies in disability, rehabilitation, healthcare, and inclusion. The 2026 proceedings continue this tradition by presenting current research and emerging perspectives from an international community working across disciplines and sectors.

candidates.title: Teacher Perspectives on Social Virtual Reality for Remote School Participation
candidates.abstract: Students experiencing emotionally based school non-attendance often lose not only instructional access but also regular social contact with school. This extended abstract reports an exploratory teacher study of a social virtual reality classroom for remote school participation. Three teachers tested the prototype and joined a facilitated focus group. Reflexive thematic analysis identified three design requirements: low-pressure participation, embodied social presence, and strong teacher orchestration within hybrid workflows. Teachers also noted possible relevance for later re-engagement with school routines, but that remains a hypothesis for future work.
