candidates.title: Roots of power: Women's decision making in farming across patrilineal and matrilineal systems in eastern Indonesia
candidates.abstract: This study examined women's involvement in vegetable farming decisions in two kinship systems: patrilineal (Southwest Sumba) and matrilineal (Malaka) in NTT province, Eastern Indonesia, involving 200 purposively selected female farmers (February–May 2023). The analytical design combined comparative descriptive analysis with MANOVA for multidimensional differences (resource access–control, information/institutions) and Mixed-Effects Logistic Regression to examine the determinants of involvement in decisions and the moderating effect of Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) knowledge. MANOVA showed simultaneous differences (Wilks' λ = 0.382; F (24,175) = 11.79; p < 0.001). In the MELR, the matrilineal system increased the odds of women's participation (OR≈2.51; p = 0.027); GAP knowledge increased the odds (OR≈1.92; p = 0.013) and interacted positively with kinship (OR≈1.62; p = 0.041). The main findings confirm that education, group involvement, and access to information strengthen women's roles, while GAP knowledge serves as a reinforcing factor, especially in the matrilineal context. Recommended policy implications include culturally sensitive GAP training tailored to patrilineal and matrilineal communities and strengthening women's access to extension services and institutions to improve the quality of vegetable-farming decisions in dryland ecosystems.

Who Betrayed John Rittmeister?
candidates.abstract: Who Betrayed John Rittmeister? unravels the mystery of betrayal, resistance and psychoanalysis in the shadow of Nazi Berlin. Rickels delves into the enigmatic circumstances surrounding the arrest and execution of John Rittmeister, a psychoanalyst and member of the resistance group Rote Kapelle. Through meticulous research and close readings of the works of Rittmeister’s colleagues and his close friend Werner Krauss, Rickels uncovers the complex interplay of psychoanalysis, political resistance and survival under the Third Reich. The book explores the adaptation of psychoanalysis to the Nazi regime, the eclectic therapies of the Göring Institute, and the haunting legacy of betrayal. At its heart, the narrative examines Krauss’s fictionalized account of their resistance efforts, offering a profound lens into the psychological and linguistic underpinnings of National Socialism. This book is essential for readers interested in the history of psychoanalysis, the Third Reich and modern Germany. It will captivate graduate students, scholars in the humanities and those apprenticed to analytic theory, as well as art world enthusiasts drawn to Rickels’ unique interdisciplinary approach.

candidates.title: Robotic handling preserves iPSC-derived vascular smooth muscle cell differentiation
candidates.abstract: To tackle the global cardiovascular disease epidemic, vascular cell culture requires scalable, efficient, and reproducible methods for differentiating cells. However, no studies have validated whether automation, essential for scale-up, preserves differentiation quality of cells. Here, we developed a differentiation protocol for induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived vascular smooth muscle cells (iVSMCs) that is applicable to both manual, and automated robotic culture. iPSC lines generated from male and female donors across various ages were used to optimize the generation of iVSMCs. iVSMCs had consistent morphology and protein expression, which were largely similar to those of primary VSMCs, including expression of myosin heavy chain-11 (MYH11), α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), transgelin (TAGLN) and calponin (CNN1). Functionally, these iVSMCs responded to the vasoconstrictor carbachol. Coupling this protocol with an automated Hamilton liquid-handling robotics system allowed the generation of iVSMCs in large quantities, that were morphologically similar to manually differentiated iVSMCs. Comparative proteomic analysis confirmed that protein expression was substantially the same between automated and manual differentiation methods. Automation markedly reduced manual labor and facilitated increased production without sacrificing cell quality. This study demonstrates the feasibility of automating iVSMC differentiation, marking a significant step towards scalable VSMC manufacture for three-dimensional applications, and for the ever-growing demands of organoid and tissue engineering applications.

candidates.title: Machine learning for wind and solar PV energy production forecasting: a systematic literature review
candidates.abstract: Abstract The growing share of renewable energy, especially solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind, increases the need for reliable power production forecasts beyond the very short term. Medium-term horizons (here defined as forecasts of at least 24 h ahead) are important for planning tasks such as market bidding, reserve sizing, and operational scheduling, but research in this area is diverse and difficult to compare due to differences in horizons, datasets, and evaluation settings. This paper presents a systematic literature review of machine learning approaches for PV and wind production forecasting with horizons $$\ge 24$$ ≥ 24 h. Following PRISMA guidelines, a Scopus search using a broad query (2978 results), followed by a refined query (69 results) and a three-stage screening process (title, abstract, and full text), resulted in 31 included studies. We extract and synthesize evidence on (i) forecast horizons and setups, (ii) model families and hybrid designs, (iii) data sources and the use of measured versus forecast weather inputs, (iv) uncertainty handling (e.g., quantiles, intervals, and scenarios), and (v) links to decision-making contexts. In addition, we propose a taxonomy to classify studies along these dimensions and support comparison across different evaluation settings. The results show that most studies focus on day-ahead and week-ahead evaluation, while 2-week and longer horizons are less common. Hybrid and ensemble approaches are widespread, while transformer-family methods appear in a smaller but visible subset. Most papers rely on measured production data, whereas fewer explicitly use forecast weather (e.g., Numerical Weather Prediction) inputs, even though weather-forecast uncertainty strongly influences multi-day performance in realistic settings. Only a limited number of studies connect forecasts to operational decisions, indicating a gap between accuracy-focused evaluation and decision value. The review highlights the need for more consistent benchmarking, more realistic weather-input evaluation (and, where relevant, other operational exogenous inputs such as curtailment), and more standard uncertainty reporting for medium-term renewable forecasting.

candidates.title: Designing the future of consciousness: A components framework and speculative implications
candidates.abstract: As technologies increasingly converge with users’ psychophysiology and mental states, perception and mind-altering are emerging as plausibly designable components of user experience. This gives rise to emergent phenomena of digitally induced altered states of consciousness (DIAL) that find application not only in therapeutic and mental health contexts but also in communication and leisure. Modern consciousness-altering technologies primarily exist as early prototypes, and their empirical research tends to constrain the context of use to instrumental functionality. Fictional narrative analysis proposes to push these limitations by considering concepts of technology in imaginary contexts, thereby examining the experiences, social rituals, and ethical issues associated with their use far beyond traditional technical scenarios. This article employs a reflexive thematic analysis of popular science fiction narratives to expand our understanding of how ASCs are integrated into HCI, considering broader sociocultural and socio-technical contexts. As a result, we identify key aspects of interaction (purpose and context) and combine their subcategories into a framework that facilitates rethinking traditional HCI, revealing potentials that remain inaccessible within clear consciousness. This framework was used to construct five themes, highlighting that the benefits of mitigating cognitive load and deepening technology-mediated communication with DIAL might entail sacrificing identity and autonomy and increasing the pressures of the modern, overcompetitive, hyper-individualistic lifestyle. Thus, the article contributes to the HCI agenda by expanding existing paradigms of interaction with mind-altering technologies and by demonstrating the use of science fiction as a powerful avenue for exploring the design space and critical inquiries about these types of interactions.

candidates.title: Project Emerge: A demonstrator for self-organizing robot teams
candidates.abstract: Aggregate computing has been studied for over a decade and is supported by multiple programming frameworks, proving suitable for simulating applications in challenging domains such as smart cities and robot swarms. Project Emerge is a toolchain for practical multi-robot demonstrations based on aggregate computing principles, validated through a public, live, interactive demo at a European Researchers’ Night event. Using a camera system and ArUco markers for localization, we show how the demonstrator coordinates mobile robots to form spatial patterns.

candidates.title: Industrial Policy, Long‐Term Orientation and Export Product Quality
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper empirically examines the impact of industrial policies on the quality of firms' export products using textual data derived from Chinese local governments' Five‐Year Plans (FYPs). The empirical results demonstrate that key industrial policies significantly contribute to upgrading export product quality, a finding that remains robust across a variety of tests. Given the endogeneity issues, we employ the interaction term of the number of late Qing cabinet ( Neige ) members who were responsible for early industry policy making and industrial capital density as IV, and the instrumented results are consistent with the baseline. Notably, we find that firms with a strong long‐term orientation (LTO) are better able to leverage industrial policies to enhance export quality. Mechanism analysis reveals that industrial policies improve export quality by encouraging innovation and promoting industrial agglomeration. Furthermore, heterogeneity analysis indicates that the positive effect of key industrial policies is more pronounced for private‐owned firms compared to foreign‐owned and state‐owned firms, for ordinary trade relative to processing trade, and in the eastern region compared to the central and western regions.

candidates.title: Teaching Disruptive Technologies in the Secondary School
candidates.abstract: This book provides a one stop shop for those interested in teaching about disruptive technologies as part of a wide variety of school subjects. It explores the technologies that are likely to have a profound influence on our society in the coming years and offers advice and guidance on how to devise, teach and assess a relevant curriculum. Divided into two parts, the first examines the nature of disruption that technologies cause. It describes in depth what each technology does, how it works, who uses it and what for, and how this might be disruptive along with positive and negative implications. The technologies include:• additive manufacture• artificial intelligence• augmented reality• Big Data• Internet of Things• quantum computing• programmable matter• neurotechnology• robotics• synthetic biology. Part two suggests practical ways teachers could ‘Look Sideways’ and collaborate to teach and assess learners aged 11-18 in these disruptive technologies so that they can successfully take up new employment opportunities and contribute fully to the debate of how those technologies affect our society.Offering comprehensive guidance on the teaching, learning and assessment of disruptive technologies, this will be valuable reading for teachers, school leaders, teacher educators and those responsible for curriculum development.

candidates.title: Inequality Within the Mobile System: Understanding the Third-Level Digital Divide Through Adverse Digital Incorporation in Rural China
candidates.abstract: As mobile media rapidly expand in the rural Global South, digital divide research is shifting from an exclusion-based to an inclusion-based perspective. Drawing on Heeks’ “adverse digital incorporation” framework and ethnographic fieldwork in rural China, this article conceptualizes the third-level digital divide, which refers to the unequal outcomes and disparate dividends derived from information and communication technologies, as the unequal extraction of value resulting from power imbalances within the mobile system. The study reveals that this adverse incorporation constitutes two closed loops of value inequality. On the one hand, smartphones break spatiotemporal boundaries to extract value through the commodification of private time, legibility and labor control, and risk-cost shifting. On the other hand, while rural residents employ strategic digital disconnection as a form of everyday resistance, which results in marginalization and reinforces value inequality. Consequently, it is essential to go beyond technical provision to enable rural residents to transform from passive content consumers into active value producers and to rebalance power within the mobile system.

candidates.title: RTSF: An open, schema-validated robot task specification format for vendor-independent description, LLM generation, and multi-platform validation of manipulator tasks
candidates.abstract: Objective: Robot task programming in manufacturing remains tightly coupled to vendor-specific languages, hindering portability and reuse. This paper presents a vendor-neutral, schema-validated format for robot task specification that enables large language model (LLM) generation and multi-robot execution without modifying the task description. Methods: The Robot Task Specification Format (RTSF) is a JSON format with nine step types covering all six control-flow constructs, governed by a JSON Schema (draft-07). A gap analysis against ten existing formats positions RTSF. Schema-guided LLM generation is evaluated on 30 task descriptions across four domains, with a prompt ablation study. A runtime architecture (recursive parser, PDDL converter, BehaviorTree.CPP converter) enables multi-backend execution. A multi-robot experiment validates six scenarios on four platforms: UR5e, Franka FR3, Kinova Gen3, and Denso Cobotta (physical robot). Results: No surveyed format combines a task-level abstraction with a formal JSON Schema, vendor-independent execution, complete control-flow coverage, and schema-guided LLM generation. The multi-robot experiment verifies identical action sequences and arguments across over 500 adapter calls on four platforms using unmodified task files. Schema-guided prompting achieves high construct recall (100% corrected validity); an independent benchmark by three external evaluators confirms generalisability. Prompt ablation confirms that disambiguation and field-name guidance rules contribute roughly equally to recall. Scalability benchmark confirms sub-second processing at 5000 steps. Conclusion: RTSF fills the gap between natural-language task descriptions and heterogeneous execution backends, enabling vendor-independent robot task programming with schema-guided LLM generation and multi-platform validation. The format, examples, scripts, and test suite (107 tests) are released under the MIT licence.

candidates.title: Beyond Comfort: Interesting Experiences and the Measurement of Well-Being in AI Care Companions
candidates.abstract: Abstract AI care companions for older adults are typically evaluated by whether they reduce loneliness, improve mood, provide companionship, or keep users mentally active. These are genuine benefits, but they do not exhaust what matters to well-being. Drawing on Lorraine Besser’s account of interesting experiences, this paper develops two reasons to treat robust cognitive engagement as a distinct design and evaluation target. First, if interestingness has experiential value not reducible to pleasure, comfort-centered measures omit an important prudential good. Second, even if interestingness is understood as a cognitively structured form of pleasure, it has a prolific character; every genuinely interesting experience opens or sustains some further possibility for engagement, although the extent of this opening varies and its development into later inquiry, activity, or relationship is contingent. Through a philosophical case study of the AI-powered care companion ElliQ, we show how a welfare-oriented companion can provide genuine benefits while failing to identify or measure this dimension of experience. Because personalized and proactive companions can shape—and sometimes displace—users’ finite time and attention, we argue that they bear a conditional, role-based, pro tanto responsibility not to narrow users’ experiential worlds. We translate this responsibility into three design principles: situated novelty, calibrated challenge, and continuity and outward transfer. These principles aim to preserve voluntary, permission-sensitive opportunities for curiosity, reflection, and engagement beyond the system itself. AI care companions should be judged not only by whether they make a person’s life more comfortable, but also by whether they help keep their world open.

candidates.title: Decentralized context models for cooperative and autonomous mobile robots
candidates.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots (AMR) are increasingly being deployed in real-world applications such as logistics, inspection, monitoring, and other demanding operations. Their capabilities become particularly valuable in cooperative settings, where heterogeneous AMRs can combine complementary strengths across different modalities (land, water, air). However, scalable cooperation requires more than navigation, task execution, and ad hoc message exchange. It requires a shared, machine-processable understanding of the current situation that is precise enough to support planning and coordination. Additionally, it must be robust enough to remain usable under uncertainty, partial connectivity, and changing mission conditions. This dissertation addresses the development of decentralized context models for cooperative AMR teams. While related research has contributed important advances in context-aware systems, ontology-based modeling, and decentralized coordination, the engineering landscape remains fragmented. Existing approaches rarely connect the systematic identification of mission-relevant context, the formal design of interoperable context representations, and the decentralized implementation and use of context information within one coherent process. To close this gap, the dissertation develops a structured engineering support framework that treats decentralized context models as explicit engineering artifacts across the phases of analysis, design, and implementation. In the analysis phase, a context identification method is introduced to derive and structure relevant context information from mission scenarios, stakeholder requirements, and system behavior. In the design phase, the work contributes design principles for distributed context modeling, a platform- and technology-independent information model, and an interoperable communication concept for cooperative AMR teams. In the implementation phase, the dissertation realizes decentralized context models through selective information distribution and uncertainty-aware consensus formation. The proposed framework and its research artifacts are evaluated through case studies and simulations involving heterogeneous teams of unmanned aerial, ground, and surface vehicles in representative cooperative scenarios. The results show that the presented approach provides a reusable methodological and architectural foundation for building decentralized context models that remain semantically consistent, interoperable, and resilient under imperfect communication and uncertainty. By systematically connecting context analysis, formal model design, and decentralized runtime realization, the dissertation establishes decentralized context models as a practical integration artifact for cooperative AMR teams.

candidates.title: Будівництво в умовах безпекових загроз: адитивні технології та автономні системи
candidates.abstract: Стаття присвячена досліджен-ню можливостей застосування адитивних технологій, префабрикації та автономних систем у будівництві в умовах воєнного стану в Україні. Обґрунтовано доцільність виготов-лення префабрикованих (модульних) захисних конструкцій на мобільних виробничих ком-плексах, розташованих поблизу зони виконан-ня робіт, із подальшим їх транспортуванням, монтажем і закріпленням роботизованими системами без безпосереднього залучення будівельників у небезпечних зонах. Встановле-но, що поєднання будівельного 3D-друку, за-водської префабрикації та автономного управління дає змогу скоротити строки ви-конання робіт, зменшити виробничі ризики та забезпечити оперативне спорудження за-хисних і фортифікаційних об’єктів, а також захистити наявну інфраструктуру. І головне, що використання автономних і безпілотних систем збереже життя і здоров’я робітників та інженерного складу. Префабрикація передбачає виготовлення будівельних елементів та модулів у заводсь-ких умовах на основі спеціально розробленої проєктної документації, з високим ступенем обробки матеріалів та попередньою інте-грацією інженерних систем, необхідних для подальшого функціонування, транспортуван-ня та монтажу. Збірні панелі, конструктивні елементи та функціональні модулі доставля-ються на будівельний майданчик, де вони зби-раються, з'єднуються між собою та кріп-ляться до непідготовленої основи за відсут-ності фундаментів та інших опорних кон-струкцій. У статті продемонстровано, що викори-стання локальних роботизованих систем знижує професійні ризики, тоді як автома-тизовані системи позамайданчикового виро-бництва, зокрема BCM та LSP, забезпечують паралельне виробництво будівельних компо-нентів і модулів у контрольованих умовах. Особлива увага приділяється мобільним ви-робничим потужностям, розташованим по-близу зони будівництва, але на безпечній відстані від основних загроз, з можливістю їх подальшого переміщення залежно від опе-раційних потреб. Розглянуто основні методи адитивного виробництва та показано, що пошарова екс-трузія наразі є одним із найперспективніших методів для застосування у масштабному будівництві. Метод передбачає укладання спеціально підготовленої швидкотверднучої бетонної суміші через екструзійне сопло відповідно до цифрової моделі. Мобільний будівельний 3D-принтер (3DCP) баштового типу, оснащений маніпулятором простої конструкції, розглядається як універсальний пристрій для виготовлення збірних захисних елементів як у заводських умовах, так і без-посередньо на будівельному майданчику. Результати дослідження підтверджують, що інтеграція адитивних технологій, мобіль-ної префабрикації та автономних систем є перспективним напрямом для захисту існую-чої інфраструктури та зведення нових за-хисних і фортифікаційних споруд. Отримані дані можуть слугувати науково-практичною базою для подальших досліджень у галузі ав-тономного транспортування, роботизовано-го монтажу, витримування бетону та вико-ристання спеціальних систем швидкого кріплення, а також для розробки національ-них будівельних норм для умов підвищеного ризику. Водночас визначено невирішені питання, пов’язані з розміщенням мобільних потужно-стей, технологічним витримуванням бетон-них конструкцій, автономним транспорту-ванням і створенням спеціальних систем кріплення префабрикованих елементів між собою та до основи

candidates.title: SKD-1: A Modular Skid-Steer Unmanned Ground Vehicle Platform for Robotics Research
candidates.abstract: This work presents the design, construction and operation of the SKD-1, a modular skid-steer unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) developed as a low-cost research platform for mobile robotics applications. The platform integrates a differential skid-steer drive system, a Raspberry Pi-based onboard computer, and a microcontroller-based control layer implemented using an STM32 microcontroller. The sensing system includes light detection and ranging (LiDAR), global navigation satellite system (GNSS), and an inertial measurement unit (IMU), enabling experiments in localization, mapping, and autonomous navigation. The software architecture is based on the Robot Operating System (ROS) 2 framework, relying on standard ROS 2 packages for perception, mapping, and path planning, with the custom hardware-interface layer being the only non-standard software component. The mechanical and electronic subsystems were designed with a modular architecture that facilitates maintenance, sensor replacement, and hardware upgrades. The primary contribution of this work is the open-hardware design, integration, and documentation of a reproducible robotics testbed, motivated by the prohibitive cost of commercial platforms in resource-constrained research contexts. Indoor and outdoor experiments—covering velocity-tracking, SLAM, and waypoint-navigation trials—demonstrate the functional integration of the sensing, actuation, and computing subsystems.

candidates.title: Algorithmic Audiences
candidates.abstract: This entry addresses the prob lem of machine vision aesthetics by looking at audiences-at what they are and how they see-at a time when computation is increasingly shaping both our world and our experience of it.Going beyond the humanist framing of audience studies (Morley 1980;Jenkins 1992; Brooker and Jermyn 2002), it starts from recognizing that multiple pro cesses of algorithmic automation are currently involved in the production and consumption of audiovisual content, be it media or art.These pro cesses end up furnishing a new category of a collective perceiver-that is, receiver of visual, auditory, and other sensory stimuli.This collective perceiver can be called "algorithmic audiences," a term that encapsulates both human and nonhuman agents.Machinic indeterminacy, whereby the identity of those agents is difficult to discretize and ascertain, is the onto-logic of this sensing ensemble.Importantly, such machinic indeterminacy precedes the era of the algorithmic Internet (where YouTube, TikTok, and text-based webpages and platforms feature huge swathes of content produced by and for machines), but it takes on a par tic u lar set of affordances in the age of advanced computation (Chun 2011).In what follows, an analy sis of the perceptive condition of the pre sent audiences of media and art (Zylinska 2023)-that is, of their experience of aisthesis (Rancière 2013)will be offered.However, this entry's aims are not only diagnostic but also propositional.Having considered the hybrid human-nonhuman ontology and the algorithmic mode of operation that characterize audiences today, we will discuss the possibility of emancipatory agency, the space of freedom within "the area of automated, programmed and programming apparatuses" (Flusser 2000, 91-92), emerging from within this hybrid complex.Aesthetic practice that engages algorithms as both its subject and its infrastructure will serve as a laboratory for investigating this possibility.First, some terminological and historical anchoring for the proposed analy sis is needed.The term "algorithmic audiences" has been in use within the interdisciplinary nexus of media studies and computer science for some time.It captures the evolution of Algorithmic Audiences

candidates.title: Analyzing Harmony in Bulgarian and Bulgarian-Influenced Choral Arrangements from the Radio to the Screen
candidates.abstract: This dissertation investigates developments in arrangements and compositions made for Bulgarian choirs between 1950 and 2025. Arrangements from Bulgaria’s communist period (1944-1989), when musical radio broadcasts were tailored to promote nationalist sentiment, eventually reached the ears of foreigners on the other side of the Iron Curtain via recordings and ensemble tours. These obrabotki (arrangements of folk tunes) became popular in the “world music” boom of the 1980s, and foreign composers soon began to create new compositions for Bulgarian choirs to sing on albums and in scores for film, television, and video games. Over time, the uses of Bulgarian choir in foreign popular media have become more musically diverse, and the themes with which it is associated have multiplied far beyond evocations of eastern Europe or women’s empowerment. After chapter 1 reviews relevant history, chapter 2 presents an exploration of tonicization practices in obrabotki written in Bulgaria during the communist period, arguing that the mode of the original melody helps determine the level of flexibility in tonicization. Chapter 3 analyzes Kate Bush’s collaboration with Trio Bŭlgarka on two albums, showing how traditional vocal techniques are given new meanings for new projects. Chapter 4 examines trends in drone, harmony, and Bulgarian language across three decades of film and television uses of Bulgarian choir, identifying areas of stasis and change in how characteristic features of obrabotki are reproduced. Chapter 5 offers two case studies of video game scores, exploring how musical norms seem to develop differently in culturally different markets. Finally, chapter 6 summarizes the findings and discusses avenues for future research. The broad chronological scope of the work provides context for the examples chosen for close musical analysis, many of which have not previously been analyzed in print.

candidates.title: Playing with Identity and Sexuality: Otome Video Games as Exploration of the Gendered Romantic Self
candidates.abstract: This dissertation examines the intersection between video game studies, queer theory, and trans studies with an autotheoretical framework. My project utilizes my position as an autistic trans queer scholar to examine the ways that otome dating simulators, which usually take the form of visual novels, can help us better understand the concepts of fictophilia and parasocialism, which in turn can shed light on the workings of transphobia and hatred-based ideologies. Fictophilia is the attraction—platonic, sexual, or romantic—that a person feels towards a fictional character; parasocialism is a kind of relationship that forms between an individual and someone with whom they believe they have a close personal connection, but in fact do not (e.g. a person who watches a Twitch streamer and believes that they are close beyond being simply a content creator and a consumer of that content). Each of the four chapters focuses on a different subtype of otome visual novels: Japanese otome visual novels (where the genre originates), Boys’ Love visual novels, North American indie otome games, and “free-to-play” or “freemium” otome games. Based on this exploration, I argue that parasocialism and fictophilia are not only connected concepts but are vital tools that can be used to better understand issues of transphobia and other forms of dehumanizing and hatred-based ideologies. In my discussion of the games I also incorporate my own experience of playing them, allowing me to take advantage of video games’ inherent embodied quality to cement broader theoretical connections. Furthermore, to gain a better understanding of the work that is required to make a video game, especially from the perspective of an indie developer, I include both my own game and a discussion of my game-making process. This thesis raises questions about gatekeeping and accessibility, not only within video game subcultures, but also within academia itself. Note: PC and Mac versions of the accompanying video game files are available.

candidates.title: World Models for Robotic Manipulation: A Survey
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Robotic manipulation depends on the ability to anticipate how actions reshape objects, contacts, and scene geometry before execution. Learned world models provide this capability by predicting task‐relevant future evolution under robot intervention, yet the term now spans latent dynamics models, action‐conditioned video generators, three‐ and four‐dimensional scene predictors, physics‐informed simulators, and predictive modules inside vision‐language‐action systems. This breadth has fragmented the literature and obscured the design choices that matter for manipulation. We survey world models for robotic manipulation through three questions: what future representation is predicted, how prediction is connected to action, and when prediction is used in the robot‐learning pipeline. We operationally define a world model as an action‐conditioned predictive system and distinguish it from perception modules, inverse models, policies, rewards, and value functions. We then organize existing work into five representation families, develop a functional taxonomy that separates integrated prediction–action models from explicit predictive planners, and characterize infrastructure roles including synthetic experience generation, candidate filtering, search‐based evaluation, learned environments, and outcome verification. We further map these roles across pretraining, post‐training, and inference adaptation, review 38 manipulation datasets, and synthesize evaluation protocols for predictive fidelity, task performance, and simulator reliability. This survey shows that world models are evolving from task‐specific dynamics predictors into predictive infrastructure for robot learning, while exposing open challenges in contact modeling, hallucination control, action alignment, and benchmarking under closed‐loop use.

candidates.title: Repositioning transanal total mesorectal excision in the robotic era
candidates.abstract: Low rectal cancer lies deep in the pelvis, close to the pelvic autonomic nerves and urogenital structures. Surgery must therefore balance oncological clearance, sphincter preservation, and functional outcomes. Total mesorectal excision (TME) remains the fundamental oncological principle across open, laparoscopic, robotic, and transanal approaches. A deep, narrow male pelvis, obesity, a very low tumor, fibrosis after neoadjuvant treatment, and restricted distal transection can make transabdominal TME technically demanding. Robotic transabdominal TME (rTME) provides three-dimensional high-definition visualization, wristed instruments, tremor filtration, and a stable operating platform. These features address several limitations of conventional laparoscopy. rTME may therefore be suitable for most patients with mid-to-low rectal cancer when distal dissection and transection remain controllable from above. Against this background, the role of transanal total mesorectal excision (TaTME) should be reassessed rather than dismissed. Current evidence neither renders TaTME obsolete nor establishes a universal advantage across all low rectal cancers. Instead, TaTME is better positioned as a selective technical complement for very low tumors, restricted distal exposure or transection, and composite difficult-pelvis scenarios. At the same time, the development of robot-assisted TaTME (R-TaTME), hybrid TaTME, single-port robotic systems, and flexible transanal platforms offers new technological avenues. These platforms may improve procedural stability and instrument dexterity during transanal surgery. This review reappraises TaTME in the robotic era, focusing on indication refinement, pathological quality, training and quality assurance, functional preservation, and platform development.

candidates.title: When Connection Feels Empty: Rethinking Consumer Loneliness Through Dual Presence in Digital Marketing
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Digital marketplaces sell connection, yet loneliness persists among their users. Marketing scholarship has largely examined loneliness as a consumer‐level deficit, studying how individuals compensate through consumption. How digital environments themselves structure the conditions under which loneliness is experienced has received less attention. This review addresses that gap by synthesizing 623 peer‐reviewed articles across marketing, psychology, communication, and information systems, using PRISMA procedures and topic modeling to map the field. Four research streams emerge, each addressing whether others feel accessible or whether one's own participation feels consequential, but rarely both together. These two perceptual conditions have been studied under different names across disciplines without being recognized as aspects of the same relational structure. When both are present, loneliness declines. When others are vivid but one's own visibility is uncertain, loneliness deepens. Digital environments can amplify this asymmetry by separating the perception of others from the perception that one's own participation registers. The review traces implications for customer engagement, brand communities, consumer‐brand relationships, and AI service design, and proposes an empirical agenda organized around how digitally mediated interaction constitutes or alters the relational conditions associated with loneliness.

candidates.title: A Modular Active–Reactive AAS Architecture for Mass-Customized Production: Validation on an Industrial-Grade Robotic Screwdriving Demonstrator
candidates.abstract: Mass-customized production introduces variants faster than certified asset models can be rebuilt. This feasibility study presents an active–reactive architecture for type-3 Asset Administration Shells (AASs) in which two submodel templates separate the reactive layer from independently deployable decision services. On the requester side, ActiveSteps represents a variant’s process sequence and references the capability each step needs, so a product’s AAS becomes a type-3 on demand. On the provider side, ActiveSkills maps offered skills to the capabilities that realize them, so one provider-core image serves every resource and only its domain services are scenario-specific. The type-2 to type-3 upgrade adds these submodels to both sides and costs one restart of the provider alone; subsequent rollouts needed none, so consumers were not interrupted. Evaluation used a university robotic screwdriving demonstrator, not a live production line. Of 104 calls for proposal, 102 were answered at a median of 4 s. Median requester activation was 8 s over 100 activations. Capability checking over 454 balanced cases with five repetitions reached an F1 of 89.6% and a 10.8% false-positive rate. An evaluation costs USD 7.0×10−4. These results support feasibility for asynchronous coordination in the evaluated cell; scalability and cross-vendor interoperability were untested.

candidates.title: Design of Deep Learning-Based Beamforming for mm-Wave Massive MIMO Systems
candidates.abstract: Millimeter waves (mmV) communication has emerged as a key enabler for wireless networks to the next generation, due to the support of ultra-high data rate with large antenna arrays. However, its practical deployment is hindered by challenges such as limited radio frequency (RF) chains, high hardware complexity and imperfect channel status information (CSI). To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel deep learning -enhanced binding (DLBF) framework for mmwave massive MIMO sys-tem. The proposed method benefits from deep neural networks to learn effective binding strategies that maximize spectral efficiency while complying with strict hard-ware restrictions. Unlike conventional bonding methods, it depends on the CSI and suffers from high computing costs, the DLBF model demonstrates strength against defects in the channel and hardware limitations. The simulation results show that the proposed DLBF method achieved significantly high spectral efficiency compared to traditional algorithms, showing its potential as a practical solution for real -world mmwave massive MIMO deployment.

candidates.title: Japanese pop culture events in Portugal: Bridging cultures and enhancing regional tourism
candidates.abstract: Abstract Japanese pop culture events in Portugal have emerged as an important platform for fostering intercultural exchange, enhancing cultural appreciation, and supporting regional tourism. This study investigates their perceived impacts on local tourism dynamics and economic development through the perspectives of organisers, participants, and other stakeholders. Drawing on a qualitative approach, the study is based on 22 in-depth interviews, which reveal that these events are perceived to improve regional attractiveness for tourists, support local economic activity through visitor flows reported by interviewees, and help mitigate tourism seasonality. The findings underscore their perceived effectiveness in promoting cultural authenticity, strengthening community engagement, and attracting younger audiences. They also suggest perceived economic benefits associated with expenditure on local goods and services, thereby potentially supporting local businesses. By focusing on the Portuguese context, which remains relatively underexplored, this study provides new insights into the role of Japanese pop culture events in cultural tourism and community development. The study offers theoretical contributions to cultural event management and practical recommendations for stakeholders seeking to maximise the cultural and economic potential of these events.

Fostering Communication, Collaboration, Critical Thinking, and Creativity via Educational Robotics
candidates.abstract: Abstract Communication, collaboration, critical thinking, and creativity—often referred to as the “4Cs”—are regarded as essential soft skills to meet the complex demands of today’s workforce. Consequently, it may be useful to facilitate the acquisition of these abilities from an early age. Meanwhile, greater attention is being given to incorporating robotics into school settings to promote useful skills. However, our understanding of how these develop through educational robotics remains limited. This experimental study aims to address this gap by investigating: (a) if tangibly programmable robots can promote the 4Cs more effectively compared to traditional methods, (b) whether differences are related to participants’ gender, age, or nature of curricular activities, and (c) the structural patterns and directional relationships among the 4Cs through path analysis. In this study, 50 preschoolers participated in 10 activities. The results showed that the experimental group outperformed the control group on the 4Cs, and gender had no significant effect on their development. Yet, it was found that age may influence communication. Additionally, the nature of activities might affect children’s skills growth. Moreover, the path analysis revealed that successful communication during robotics activities might lead to effective collaboration, which in turn may influence both critical thinking and creativity. Overall, these preliminary, exploratory findings offer valuable insights into the potential of robotics as a powerful tool for promoting 21st-century skills in early childhood education.

candidates.title: Enhancing social and linguistic skills in children with autism: A semi‐randomized controlled clinical trial of a virtual reality‐based communicative rehabilitation programme
candidates.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by persistent deficits in social communication, and conventional therapies often struggle to facilitate the generalization of these skills to real-world settings. This study aimed to determine the effectiveness of a virtual reality (VR)-based communication rehabilitation intervention as a supplement to conventional treatment for improving the linguistic and social communication skills of Arabic-speaking Egyptian children with ASD. A clinical trial with a pretest-posttest control group design was employed, wherein 60 children aged 4-6 years with mild to moderate ASD were assigned to either VR plus conventional therapy (Group I, n = 30) or conventional therapy alone (Group II, n = 30). Over 6 months, participants received 2 weekly 30-min sessions. Outcomes were measured at baseline, immediately post-intervention and at a 3-month follow-up using the Preschool Language Scale-Fourth Edition, the Childhood Autism Rating Scale-Second Edition and an ASD Social Skills Scale. Group I demonstrated statistically significant improvements in receptive and expressive language ages (p < .001) and total social skills scores (p < .001) compared to Group II. Crucially, these therapeutic gains were sustained at the 3-month follow-up with no significant deterioration (p > .05). VR-based communication rehabilitation is a highly effective and sustainable intervention for supplementing language and social skills in young children with ASD. Its integration into clinical practice provides a scalable, engaging and culturally adaptable platform for neurodevelopmental care.

candidates.title: Governing AI at the clinical threshold: a grounded theory framework for responsible AI deployment in mindfulness-based mental health
candidates.abstract: AI-powered platforms for mental health delivery are scaling rapidly into contexts previously governed by trained human practitioners—without empirically grounded frameworks to guide their ethical deployment, manage adverse effects risk, or address the structural design failures that make them harmful to vulnerable populations. This constructivist grounded theory study examined how expert mindfulness clinicians and teachers conceptualize governance failures, societal harms, and design risks in AI-mediated mental health delivery. Fourteen practitioners—representing six contemplative and clinical traditions, with experience ranging from 8 to 60 years—were recruited via purposive and theoretical sampling and interviewed using a semi-structured protocol. Data were analyzed through iterative open, axial, and selective coding by a four-member team, with theoretical saturation confirmed at N = 13. Analysis generated the Bounded Convergence Framework (BCF), a three-zone governance model organizing AI deployment into an inner zone of irreducibly human clinical functions, a practitioner-governed boundary zone defined by three non-negotiable threshold conditions, and an outer zone of legitimate AI-assisted functions. Sixteen governance principles were identified, with particular implications for contraindication screening, crisis escalation architecture, AI identity disclosure, and the protection of adolescent and trauma-exposed populations. The BCF offers the first empirically grounded governance framework for AI deployment in mindfulness-based mental health delivery, with direct implications for platform developers, health service administrators, regulators, and clinical practitioners navigating this rapidly expanding and underregulated domain.

candidates.title: Citation landscape and research themes of robotic-assisted total hip arthroplasty: a bibliometric analysis of the 100 most-cited English-language publications in the Web of Science Core Collection
candidates.abstract: Robotic-assisted total hip arthroplasty (ra-THA) has received increasing academic attention. This bibliometric study aimed to identify the 100 most-cited English-language articles related to ra-THA indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (WOSCC) and to characterize their citation patterns, evidence levels, research themes, and collaboration networks. The WOSCC was searched for English-language articles and reviews related to ra-THA. The retrieved records were ranked by total citation count, screened according to predefined eligibility criteria, and the 100 most-cited articles were included for analysis. Data on publication year, citation count, journal, authorship, country, institution, keywords, document type, and level of evidence were extracted. Citation density, year-normalized citation indicators, Mann-Kendall trend analysis, Spearman correlation analysis, and bibliometric visualizations were used to evaluate citation patterns, temporal trends, research themes, and collaboration networks. The 100 included articles were published between 2008 and 2025. Publication output and citation frequency showed increasing tendencies within this highly cited cohort. The United States contributed the largest number of articles and citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The Journal of Arthroplasty, Clinical Orthopaedics and Related Research, and The Bone & Joint Journal were major publication sources. Keyword analysis indicated that surgical accuracy, navigation, clinical outcomes, and procedure-related risks were frequent research themes. No statistically significant association was observed between level of evidence and citation count within the selected cohort. Among the 100 most-cited English-language WOSCC-indexed articles retrieved using the specified search strategy, ra-THA research showed increasing citation attention over time. The most frequently represented themes were surgical accuracy, navigation, clinical outcomes, and procedure-related risks. These findings provide a bibliometric overview of the influential citation landscape and thematic development of ra-THA research.

Animal-Assisted Therapy in Dementia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Cognitive, Affective, and Behavioral Outcomes
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) are common and represent major drivers of caregiver burden and healthcare utilization. Animal-assisted therapy (AAT) is used as a non-pharmacological intervention in dementia care, yet quantitative evidence of its efficacy remains inconsistent. We systematically evaluated the effects of AAT on cognitive, affective, and behavioral outcomes in individuals with dementia. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched seven electronic databases from inception through 27 September 2025 for studies evaluating AAT in dementia. Randomized and non-randomized controlled studies were included in quantitative synthesis. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 and ROBINS-I tools. Random-effects meta-analyses used standardized mean differences (SMDs), with sensitivity, influence, subgroup, and publication bias analyses conducted where appropriate. Results: Fifty-nine studies met inclusion criteria, including 24 controlled studies with 1881 participants. AAT was associated with reduced overall BPSD severity, although this effect was sensitive to study quality and was not retained after excluding high-risk studies. AAT significantly improved depressive symptoms (SMD, −0.79, 95%CI, −1.33 to −0.26) and cognitive performance (SMD, 1.17; 95%CI, 0.31 to 1.79), with substantial heterogeneity; both effects persisted after excluding studies at high or serious risk of bias. No significant effects were observed for agitation, quality of life, or activities of daily living. Benefits were observed primarily in live animal interventions; robotic subgroups comprised a few studies and were underpowered to detect an effect. Conclusions: AAT may confer meaningful benefits for mood and cognitive engagement in dementia, particularly with live animals, but confidence is limited by methodological heterogeneity and the predominance of studies at moderate to serious risk of bias.

candidates.title: Integrated sensing and actuation for a predominantly-flexible underwater robot
candidates.abstract: Soft robots offer a compliant and inherently safer alternative to rigid platforms for underwater exploration and close-proximity interaction. However, many existing underwater soft robots still depend on bulky external power/pressure supplies or rigid supporting modules, which limits autonomy and complicates the integration of sensing and actuation. This paper investigates a predominantly flexible underwater robotic agent enabled by flexible energy storage and low-voltage ionic actuation. A self-contained, multi-modal ionic polymer–metal composite (IPMC) robot is developed using a flexible battery pack as the onboard power source. By exploiting the battery current response to contact induced load variations at the IPMC actuator, the same integrated system provides both propulsion and tactile perception without adding discrete sensors. Experiments demonstrate untethered multi-modal locomotion with gait switching and show that even the weakest lateral contact produces a 14.1% change in the measured current-response feature, supporting reliable tactile-state discrimination.

candidates.title: From Clinical Technique to Interprofessional Implementation and Intelligent Integration: A Bibliometric Analysis of the Interdisciplinary Expansion of Robot‐Assisted Spine Surgery
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Robot-assisted spine surgery (RASS) has expanded beyond technical accuracy towards interprofessional, perioperative, and AI-driven implementation, yet this interdisciplinary evolution has not been systematically characterised. METHODS: We analysed 327 Web of Science Core Collection publications (2006-2026) at the intersection of RASS and perioperative, collaborative, or educational research. Analyses included co-authorship networks, keyword co-occurrence, co-citation mapping, bibliographic coupling, citation-burst detection, Callon strategic mapping, and dual-map overlays, performed in VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Bibliometrix. Ethical approval was not required as only de-identified bibliographic records were analysed. RESULTS: = 0.8762), peaking at 62 publications in 2025; the partial year 2026 (indexed only to the 4 February 2026 search date) was excluded from all growth-rate and trendline modelling. The United States (n = 137) and China (n = 57) dominated output. Dual-map analysis indicated citation flows into the (broad) Health/Nursing/Medicine domain. Keyword bursts identified artificial intelligence (strength = 3.13), deep learning (2.01), and augmented reality (1.75) as the most recent (2023-2025) research frontiers. Rehabilitation robotics remained bibliographically isolated from the surgical core. CONCLUSIONS: The published literature on RASS shows a measurable thematic shift from procedural-accuracy validation towards perioperative-implementation and intelligent-integration topics; whether this bibliometric shift reflects a corresponding change in clinical practice cannot be determined from publication data. These patterns nonetheless motivate investment in cross-disciplinary consortia, AI-competency frameworks, and attention to implementation equity.

candidates.title: Nonreciprocal Swarmalators With Reconfigurable and Controllable Formations for Robot Collectives
candidates.abstract: We use the swarmalator model to enable nonreciprocal coupling between agents and demonstrate that by controlling these time‐varying interactions between the agents, the collective can be made to exhibit controllable shape formation, motion, obstacle avoidance, and object transport, all of which are realized by modulating the asymmetric coupling between agents. Target formations are represented as forward‐invariant geometric sets whose boundaries encode desired shapes, and safety and formation constraints are enforced through quadratic programs that minimally alter the swarmalator model‐induced velocities. Our framework supports a broad class of two‐ and three‐dimensional formations, including smooth and non‐convex shapes, annular and shell‐like structures, and polyhedron geometries with sharp corners that are realized through piecewise barrier functions. We also demonstrate that time‐varying barrier functions can be used to enable continuous morphing between formations, and that emergent and controllable motion through mazes and cluttered environments can be achieved while the collective remains in a desired formation. Finally, we show an integrated demonstration that combines collective splitting, parallel navigation, and contact‐driven transport and assembly of objects to highlight how functional tasks can be achieved by systematically reconfiguring the system's constraints and objectives while having each agent remain subject to the swarmalator model.

candidates.title: Diffusion-transformer hybrid model for robust Taijiquan motion assessment
candidates.abstract: Traditional Tai Chi (Taijiquan) assessment suffers from subjectivity and low precision. This study develops a generative artificial intelligence (GAI)-based system integrating High-Resolution Network (HRNet), Vision Transformer for Human Pose Estimation (ViTPose), and diffusion models for intelligent posture evaluation. The framework enables pose reconstruction, motion generation, and semantic scoring. Evaluated on the UMONS-TAICHI dataset, the model achieves Mean Per Joint Position Error (MPJPE) = 7.142, smoothness index = 0.911, and Pose Completion Ratio (PCR) = 96.248. It maintains PCR > 93.957 under 10–40% occlusion, outperforming baseline models. The system accurately evaluates complex movements with coordination and rhythm scores > 0.90. This GAI-driven approach provides an objective, robust tool for Taijiquan digitalization and intelligent training.

candidates.title: From ‘Old Man Yells at Cloud’ to Geronto-Futurism: Co-Imagining Holography and Aging
candidates.abstract: This article explores the discursive, industrial, artistic, and practical interconnections between older people, aging, and holography, arguing that their nexus mutually shapes how both concepts are culturally constituted. Methodologically, the paper utilizes a discourse and representation analysis to examine a heterogeneous corpus of actual wave-optic holography and pseudo-holographic lens-optic phantasmagorias-collectively addressed as "(quasi-)holographic" phenomena. Dissolving the boundaries between cultural fiction and industrial technology, the analysis tracks two central thematic clusters revolving around exclusion and inclusion to interrogate how older adults are integrated into techno-social futures. The paper demonstrates that while older individuals are frequently subjected to exclusionary transhumanist logics or paternalistic, resource-scarcity-driven care practices, they also emerge as active agents of inclusive technology. By analyzing cases ranging from speculative science fiction to real-world care appliances, this study maps a neglected intersection in media and aging studies. Ultimately, it introduces the concept of "geronto-futurist" interventions. These practices not only expose the marginalized position of older adults in technological imaginations but actively reshape techno-futurities. By introducing an age lens to media practices, this article contributes to broader discussions of techno-social equality, highlighting how notions of later life actively shape contemporary understandings of digitality.

candidates.title: Regulated liquid metal via semiconductor valve toward highly stretchable topological circuits
candidates.abstract: Wearable electronics with complex circuits and three-dimensional (3D) structure are indispensable to advanced next-generation flexible technologies like e-skins and soft robotics. However, fabricating 3D flexible electronics remains challenging, primarily due to the difficulty in obtaining highly stretchable materials with precise current control and complex topological structures. This work reports a unidirectional conductive semiconductor valve in liquid metals (LM-SV) constructed via interfacial barrier engineering to enable soft, complex topological circuits. The LM-SV exhibits ultrahigh stretchability (~1000% strain), robust unidirectional conductivity over 1000 cycles at 500% strain, and stable operation across wide temperature ( − 5–100 °C) and frequency (1 Hz – 5 MHz) ranges. Switching voltages (0.43—0.80 V) are conveniently tunable through LM composition modulation. Leveraging these features, LM-SV circuits can be topologically reconfigured from 2D layouts into 3D architectures with real-time functional switching. Furthermore, a wirelessly powered stretchable logic circuit demonstrates the potential of this LM-SV strategy for advanced flexible electronic systems. Fabricating 3D flexible electronics is challenging due to the difficulty in obtaining highly stretchable materials with precise current control and complex topological structures. Here, the authors report a unidirectional conductive semiconductor valve in liquid metals for soft, complex topological circuits.

candidates.title: AI-assisted literary-to-song adaptation: a practice-based study of literary interpretation in a text-to-audio workflow
candidates.abstract: This qualitative practice-based digital humanities article examines AI-assisted literary-to-song adaptation. GenAI research has addressed writing support, music generation, literary analysis and creative work, with less attention to literary judgement in generated audio and post-production. The corpus comprises 32 songs developed by a single creator, largely based on H. P. Lovecraft and produced in a post-punk/indie-rock idiom through close reading, researcher-written lyrics, ChatGPT-supported revision, Udio text-to-audio generation and human-directed assembly. Two cases are analysed: ‘The Viol Screams’ adapts The Music of Erich Zann and ‘Whispers from Yuggoth’ brings together selected sonnets from Fungi from Yuggoth. Benchmarking, listener testing and human-only comparison fall outside scope. The analysis traces source selection, lyric development, generation, evaluation, repair and post-production, focusing on textual transformation, interpretive emphasis and production intervention. Across the cases, generated audio was selected and assembled using literary, musical and technical criteria, while source structure affected human work across stages. Researchers in digital humanities and human-AI creative practice can use the source-to-song workflow heuristic and lyric-strategy typology to document how literary meaning moves into generated sound. Distributed interpretive control gives adaptation and popular music scholars a case-derived concept for examining how interpretive priorities remain active in lyric, vocal, sectional and production decisions.

candidates.title: From the Thoracoscope to the Robot: The Evolving Landscape of Minimally Invasive Pulmonary Surgery
candidates.abstract: Surgical resection is the main curative option for non-small-cell lung cancer. Pulmonary resections have historically been performed through a highly morbid open thoracotomy. Minimally invasive approaches to pulmonary resection have revolutionized the field with reduced perioperative morbidity, including less postoperative pain, length-of-stay, and complications, while potentially enhancing oncologic outcomes. In its current generation, robotically performed video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (R-VATS) offers numerous advantages over traditional VATS and is increasingly becoming the standard of care. In this review, we highlight the technical and clinical advantages of R-VATS compared to VATS and traditional thoracotomy. We reflect on emerging advancements in the utilization of the minimally invasive platform for single-anesthetic marking and resection of pulmonary nodules, the integration of artificial intelligence and radiomics to augment preoperative planning, and the expanding role of single-incision robotic surgery. Lastly, we discuss the financial considerations of implementing a robotic thoracic platform and identify opportunities to optimize costs.

candidates.title: Phased genetic algorithm for simultaneous morphology and controller optimization in soft robots
candidates.abstract: The tight coupling between morphology, material distribution, actuator layout, and control makes soft robot design a high-dimensional and expensive optimization problem when body and controller are co-designed. In this paper, “co‑design” refers specifically to morphology evolution with per‑candidate reinforcement learning of control, not to the joint genetic evolution of brain and body. We propose a phased genetic algorithm (GA) that evolves voxel‑based morphologies; each candidate is evaluated by training an independent PPO controller under a fixed budget. Three key mechanisms are introduced: 1) a task-aware prior initialization that injects weakly biased, physically meaningful morphology templates into the initial population; 2) a large-block crossover operator (exchanging 2 $$\times$$ 2 or 3 $$\times$$ 3 voxel blocks) that preserves functional morphology modules; and 3) a phased evolutionary schedule that balances exploration and stabilization. Compared with four baselines, the proposed method achieves competitive overall performance, with clear advantages on Climber-v0 and Thrower-v0 and faster convergence on Walker-v0. Not applicable.

candidates.title: Learning to carve nature at its joints: the development of hierarchical event structures in perception and action
candidates.abstract: Adults have a semantically discretised, event-based perception of reality – such that events and goals are both hierarchically structured and have a beginning, middle and end. Here, we consider how we first develop the ability to parse reality into discrete units - as we learn, to use Plato’s phrase, to ‘carve nature at its joints’. Central to this process is the ability to make predictions on hierarchical timescales. We consider two aspects of predictability: first, a child’s capacity to use predictability to inform how they observe events as they unfold; and second, children’s capacity to actively generate predictable sequences of behaviour. We highlight two themes that are, we argue, common across both observation and action. First, flat (i.e. non-hierarchical) predictability initially increases over development, before decreasing as hierarchical predictability (i.e. nested, multi-level goals) increases. Second, learnt regularities in low-level environmental data (e.g., movement, contrast, over fine-grained timescales) feed into our internal predictions of higher-order events (e.g., goals, over more coarse-grained timescales). In sum, over development, children construct increasingly elaborate hierarchies in the observation and generation of events.

candidates.title: Extended depth‐of‐field reflected‐light microscopy with a low‐cost robotic microscope and Fiji focus stacking: Workflow integration and baseline evaluation
candidates.abstract: Optical reflected-light microscopy is widely used in mechanical and tribological testing laboratories, but its limited depth of field (DOF) restricts imaging of non-planar post-test surfaces when high-NA objectives are needed to resolve fine features. Here we present a low-cost robotic microscopy system (bill of materials around USD 300) that extends depth of field through controlled axial scanning and computational focus stacking. Built on the OpenFlexure platform and using open-source software tools, the system captures z-stacks and reconstructs all-in-focus micrographs in Fiji (ImageJ distribution) using extended-depth-of-field (EDOF) fusion engines. The workflow is demonstrated on mechanically tested surfaces (scratches and indentations), providing all-in-focus visualisation of features such as scratch lips, pile-up, indentation boundaries and microcracks on reflective textured surfaces, with Scanning Electron Microscopy used for cross-checking of feature detectability. Baseline characterisation includes operational DOF and resolving-power measurements, a geometric-distortion assessment using a micrometric grid target, and a time-cost analysis of stack acquisition. Comparative evaluation of three widely used fusion methods (Sobel, variance and complex wavelets) using image-quality metrics and visual inspection indicates that complex-wavelet fusion yields sharper reconstructions and improved edge preservation relative to Sobel and variance, at the expense of higher computation time. Finally, we summarise practical constraints and observed failure modes under representative conditions, providing baseline guidance for routine use, including deployment close to mechanical test stations. LAY DESCRIPTION: Low-cost reflected-light microscopy has shallow depth of field when high-NA objectives image rough surfaces. We demonstrate a fully open (∼USD 300) OpenFlexure-based robotic microscope with an end-to-end Fiji focus-stacking workflow that produces all-in-focus micrographs of scratches and indentations, cross-checked against SEM. Baseline characterisation covers DOF, resolving power, geometric distortion, and acquisition-time effects. Complex-wavelet fusion outperforms Sobel and variance in sharpness at higher computation time. Practical constraints are identified for post-test failure analysis.

candidates.title: Anthropomorphic Non‐Fungible Token Characters in Destination Marketing: How Psychological Distance and Playfulness Drive Impulsive Travel Intentions
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Destinations are increasingly adopting Non‐Fungible Tokens (NFTs) as innovative tools for brand communication and visitor engagement in digital tourism contexts. Drawing on Construal Level Theory (CLT), we examine how the anthropomorphic (ANT) design of NFT characters influences tourists' impulsive travel intentions and whether customization strengthens this effect. In two online experiments, we tested a sequential mediation model linking ANT to impulsive travel intention through psychological distance (PD) and perceived playfulness. The results show that highly anthropomorphic NFT characters increase psychological proximity, which subsequently increases impulsive travel intentions. Moreover, customization significantly strengthens this indirect effect. This study extends research on digital destination marketing while offering practical guidance for designing effective NFT‐based tourism strategies.

candidates.title: The Process as the Purpose: Thermography, Stratigraphy, and Ephemeral Communal Mound-Building at the Late Preceramic Period Huaca Herrera de Guañape, Virú Valley, Peru
candidates.abstract: This article addresses early monumentality through the first scientific investigation of Huaca Herrera de Guañape in the Virú Valley, Peru. Methodologically, UAV-acquired infrared thermography identified subsurface architectural layouts, guiding the sampling strategy for subsequent excavation. Stratigraphic analysis and Bayesian modeling then reveal that the terminal phases of mound construction involved massive accumulations formed within extremely brief windows. These episodic construction events also reflect a pattern of horizontal expansion distinct from the vertical accretional models commonly observed in other non-hierarchical Andean contexts. By revealing the construction process, Huaca Herrera offers an opportunity to examine the social logic of monumentality through the act of building. Current work suggests that the building process could function as a social mechanism for communal gathering and cooperative goal-attainment within small-scale societies. At Huaca Herrera, the communal act of construction itself served as the primary purpose of these collaborative social endeavors.

candidates.title: ‘Passing’ the baton of trauma: Queer failure of the Women’s Sport Policy Working Group’s anti-trans ‘position’
candidates.abstract: Engaging in critical rhetorical theory and methodology, we interrogate the contemporary landscape of anti-trans backlash in women’s sport. Specifically, we read the ‘TERF wars’ (Pearce et al.) across critiques of biofeminism (Pape) and whiteness (Fischer) while drawing upon critical social science research into trauma-bonding, bullying, and the structural impacts of gender verification policies. Our analysis focuses on the Women’s Sports Policy Working Group (WSPWG), offering a trauma-informed reading of the WSPWG’s ‘Position’ statement to illuminate how lesbian female athletes who were previously slandered for failing to meet femininity norms in sport are unable to overcome that trauma to recognize and create competitive space for trans-feminine or intersex/DSD athletes today. Ultimately, we argue that organizations like the WSPWG, like other actors in this current transgender sport panic, manifest a queer failure: rather than recognize that their experiences as ‘mannish’ lesbians index a set of deeply queer paradoxes in sport, these survivors of the gender-binary trauma that impacts nearly all women in sport reveal a blindness that prevents them from extending the recognition they once demanded. By remaining captive to the trauma of ‘passing’ as women, the WSPWG passes this trauma along to the next generation of women–be they cis, queer, trans, or just fast, strong, successful, and thus threatening in sport today.
